# Test if the interaction block as a whole is statistically significant
# Identify the indices of the interaction terms within your model coefficients
interaction_indices <- grep("baseline_mental_health.*:imd_quintile", names(m3_interaction$best))

# Run the multivariate Wald test
wald_result <- WaldMult(m3_interaction, pos = interaction_indices)
print(wald_result)


# Conceptual framework for a Monte Carlo Power Check
calculate_trajectory_power <- function(target_N, loops = 500) {
  significant_results <- 0
  
  for(i in 1:loops) {
    # 1. Simulate data matching your exact categorical distributions
    # Injecting a 5% true effect size for the interaction term
    simulated_data <- generate_sim_data(N = target_N, true_interaction_effect = 0.05)
    
    # 2. Try fitting the model (wrapped in tryCatch to handle convergence drops)
    fit <- tryCatch({
      Jointlcmm(fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, mixture = ~ observation_time, 
                random = ~ observation_time, subject = "patient_id",
                classmb = ~ baseline_bp + baseline_dm + baseline_mental_health * imd_quintile,
                survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
                hazard = "3-quant-splines", hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
                data = simulated_data, ng = 3, verbose = FALSE)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    # 3. Check if the interaction term p-value is < 0.05
    if(!is.null(fit)) {
      p_val <- extract_interaction_p(fit)
      if(p_val < 0.05) significant_results <- significant_results + 1
    }
  }
  
  # Return empirical statistical power
  return(significant_results / loops)
}
